research_question: Can calibration on molecule-disjoint experimental SAR-linked MMP transformation-site proxies control empirical missed-proxy risk for atom explanation sets on held-out activity-cliff pairs?
proxy_boundary: Experimental SAR-linked transformation-site proxy; not causal, complete, mechanistic, or expert ground truth.

source.data_lineage: MoleculeACE benchmark data derived from ChEMBL v29

split.development: deterministic 80/20 split of training-only MMP/scaffold connected components
split.leakage_rule: No canonical molecule may occur in both calibration and test; neither CRC split is used for model selection.

mmp.activity_cliff: absolute measured pActivity difference > 1.0 and the frozen reference-pipeline MoleculeACE similarity rule (Morgan Tanimoto >= 0.9, generic-scaffold Tanimoto >= 0.9, or canonical-SMILES normalized Levenshtein similarity >= 0.9)
mmp.cut: exactly one non-ring heavy-atom single bond
mmp.pair: identical canonical attachment-labelled core and different variable fragments; a deterministic maximum-cardinality, maximum-weight graph matching makes molecules disjoint within each CRC split
mmp.ambiguity_resolution: match the auditable reference-pipeline rdMMPA FragmentMol(maxCuts=1) rule: maximize fragment heavy atoms and break a size tie lexically; among pair mappings maximize common-core heavy atoms, and exclude incompatible tied mappings
mmp.main_proxy: variable fragment plus core attachment atom on both molecules, then automorphism closure
sensitivities: one-hop expansion of main proxy with automorphism closure

predictor.resource_fallback: complete all 11 targets with seed 42 and report the limitation

explanation.candidate_domain: disjoint union of atoms in A and B
explanation.tie_policy: include all atoms tied at the boundary
